executive_summary: The day’s biggest advanced-transportation developments centered on drone and autonomy systems: DOT and FAA launched the federal eVTOL pilot program in Texas with Joby beginning flights, while U.S. defense reporting highlighted live counter-drone testing and new military uncrewed aircraft development. Internationally, China set a 2030 target for broad self-driving deployment, Spain authorized autonomous drone operations and issued its first L4 robotaxi permit, and Canada and Ukraine announced a 100-year partnership including drones and defense cooperation.
what_to_watch: FAA and DOT implementation details on Texas eIPP flights, including whether any additional routes, aircraft, or local partners are added next.
Whether U.S. agencies or DoD expand counter-drone deployments or tests tied to mass gatherings, border security, or military exercises.
Spain’s new L4 robotaxi permit rollout, including when the first public passenger service starts and whether more cities follow.

Trump Administration Wins.title: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Celebrates Launch of Federal eVTOL Pilot Program in Texas to Unlock the Future of Flight | US Department of Transportation
Trump Administration Wins.summary: DOT and FAA launched the federal eVTOL pilot program in Texas, with Joby beginning flights as part of the first operational activity. The program is meant to gather real-world data for future air-taxi rules and planning, while Texas agencies and industry partners line up infrastructure and testing support.
Trump Administration Wins.section: eVTOL Integration Pilot Program and AAM
Trump Administration Wins.eo_section_summary: accelerating safe U.S. eVTOL deployment through eIPP
Trump Administration Wins.win_explanation: The DOT and FAA launched the federal eVTOL pilot program in Texas and Joby began the first flights under it. The program will help the United States gather operating data for air-taxi rules and planning, supporting future commercial service and aviation jobs.

UAS Security and C-UAS.title: US and Indian armies kick off ‘Yudh Abhyas 2026’, counter-drone systems being used for first time; Sergio
UAS Security and C-UAS.summary: The U.S. and Indian armies opened Yudh Abhyas 2026 in Alaska and used counter-drone systems in the exercise for the first time. The drills add another layer of bilateral training focused on detecting and defeating UAS threats.

UAS Security and C-UAS.title: MAI Suspends All International Flights From Mandalay Airport Following Drone Attack
UAS Security and C-UAS.summary: Drone-related airspace disruptions continued to ripple through civil aviation, including Mandalay airport’s suspension of international flights after a drone attack and other reports of airspace closures or firefighting interruptions. These are security and airspace incidents, not combat stories.

also_covered.source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

Military.title: 'Save Him!' RFE/RL Captures Chaos After Russian Strike On Ukrainian Shops
Military.summary: Several records describe Russian drone and missile attacks affecting civilians, infrastructure, and travel in and around Ukraine and neighboring airspace. These are active-war reports and belong in Military rather than C-UAS.

Military.title: U.S. Tests Perseus Harpe Interceptor for Low Collateral Defense Against Small Drone Attacks
Military.summary: U.S. defense reporting points to a live test of the Perseus Harpe interceptor and other counter-drone capability-building efforts, including Pentagon testing at Yuma and Navy interest in systems such as VAMPIRE. Several related items describe new training, prototypes, and contracts for low-collateral C-UAS.

Military.title: General Atomics presenta Wildfire, il successore di Reaper.
Military.summary: General Atomics unveiled Wildfire, a new uncrewed combat aircraft pitched as a Reaper successor. Other coverage in the set points to similar high-end military drone-development stories, but this is the cleanest lead for the story.

Autonomous Vehicles.title: China targets mass deployment of self-driving vehicles by 2030
Autonomous Vehicles.summary: Reuters reports that China is targeting broad deployment of self-driving vehicles by 2030, signaling a national push to scale automated driving. In the same cycle, Spain issued the first L4 robotaxi permit for Uber, WeRide, and Avomo, while Tesla’s Cybercab continued public demonstrations in New York and Japan.

Other Advanced Transportation.title: NASA to Test How X-59 Sonic Boom Affects People in Cities

International.title: Canada-Ukraine declaration for a 100-year partnership
International.summary: Canada and Ukraine announced a 100-year partnership that includes drones, defense, and energy cooperation. The package also overlaps with separate reports of drone-manufacturing and counter-drone production plans tied to the same bilateral relationship.

International.title: Indonesia Absorbs $7.3 Billion High-Speed Rail Debt, Testing Fiscal Discipline Limits
International.summary: Indonesia’s decision to absorb $7.3 billion in high-speed rail debt is the clearest new rail development in the set. Related items across India and the U.K. point to continued bullet-train and rail-infrastructure buildout, but most are either planning updates or promotional coverage.

International.title: AESA authorises CATEC to autonomously manage its drone operations
International.summary: Spain’s AESA authorized CATEC to autonomously manage drone operations, one of several international civil-drone developments in the records. Other items cover new testing hubs and operational approvals in India, Australia, and Ireland.
